title: Watched by the World's Malignant Eye
description: Watched by the World's Malignant Eye in Tonic Solfa to SELENA, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 319.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to SELENA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Watched by the world's ma-lig-nant eye, Who load us with re-proach and shame. As ser-vants of the Lord most High, As zeal-ous for his glo-rious name, We ought in all his paths to move, With ho-ly fear and hum-ble love.

lines: Watched by the world's malignant eye,
Who load us with reproach and shame.
As servants of the Lord most High,
As zealous for his glorious name,
We ought in all his paths to move,
With holy fear and humble love.
That wisdom, Lord, on us bestow,
To stop the mouth of every foe,
While, upright both in life and heart,
The proofs of godly fear we give,
And show them how the Christians live.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to SELENA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
